summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) was admitted for right upper quadrant pain and fever, concerning for recurrent cholangitis. Despite negative blood cultures and an MRCP showing no biliary dilation or acute cholangitis, she was treated with IV meropenem due to clinical signs of infection. Her symptoms improved, liver enzymes trended downward, and she became afebrile. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic therapy, and she was transitioned to ertapenem to complete a 14-day course. Diuretics were restarted, and lactulose was increased for hepatic encephalopathy prophylaxis. She was discharged home with home health support, instructions to continue all chronic medications, and follow-up with hepatology and for colonoscopy screening.
